title: Nonlocal nonstabilizerness for slightly entangled quantum many-body states
abstract: Nonlocal nonstabilizerness quantifies the irreducible magic resource encoded in bipartite entanglement, but its evaluation is generally hindered by a highly nonconvex optimization over local unitary transformations. Here we propose a Schmidt-reference-state framework that replaces this optimization by a direct construction from the sorted Schmidt spectrum. We conjecture that the nonlocal stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) is given by the SRE of the corresponding reference state, and support this conjecture through analytical and numerical evidences. Our framework makes nonlocal nonstabilizerness efficiently accessible for weakly entangled many-body states whenever the entanglement spectrum is available. Applying it to Haar-random states, critical spin chains, and PXP dynamics, we show that nonlocal SRE captures nonstabilizer structures in the entanglement spectrum that are invisible to conventional entanglement measures. Our results establish entanglement spectra as a powerful window into irreducible nonstabilizer correlations, opening a broadly applicable route to studying nonlocal magic resources of quantum many-body systems in and out of equilibrium.
summary: The paper introduces a novel Schmidt-reference-state framework to calculate nonlocal nonstabilizerness, a key resource measure in quantum many-body physics. This method bypasses intractable optimization problems by relating the true value to an easily computable reference state derived from the entanglement spectrum. It establishes entanglement spectra as a powerful diagnostic tool for understanding irreducible correlations in both equilibrium and dynamic systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is efficiently calculating 'nonlocal nonstabilizerness,' a quantum resource quantifying irreducible magic encoded in bipartite entanglement, which involves solving a highly nonconvex optimization problem.
main_result: The authors propose a Schmidt-reference-state framework that allows for the efficient calculation of nonlocal SRE directly from the sorted Schmidt spectrum, capturing nonstabilizer correlations invisible to conventional measures.
method: They introduce a canonical reference state derived from the sorted Schmidt coefficients and conjecture that the true minimum is achieved by this state, bypassing complex local unitary optimization over $SU(d_A) \otimes SU(d_B)$.
model_or_system: The analysis applies to bipartite pure quantum many-body states ($\vert\psiangle_{AB}$), with applications demonstrated on Haar-random states, critical spin chains (Ising/XXZ models), and dynamics in Rydberg atom arrays.
key_observables: Nonlocal $\alpha$-Stabilizer Rényi Entropy ($M_{	ext{NL}}^\alpha$), the entanglement spectrum ($\{\lambda_i\}$), and the reference state SRE ($M_{	ext{ref}}^\alpha$).
important_parameters: The Rényi index $\alpha$, the Schmidt rank ($\chi$), and the specific structure of the entanglement spectrum.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the minimum nonlocal nonstabilizerness is achieved by the reference state constructed from the sorted Schmidt spectrum, a conjecture supported by necessary optimality conditions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the nonlocal SRE calculated via manifold optimization against the reference state prediction for various entanglement spectra. Figure 2 plots $M_{NL}^2$ for rank-4 spectra, identifying global maximizers.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the computational bottleneck of nonlocal nonstabilizerness, then introduces and rigorously supports the Schmidt-reference-state framework by showing its equivalence to manifold optimization results. Finally, it applies this tool to various physical models like critical chains and fermionic systems.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, computationally tractable diagnostic tool for quantifying subtle quantum correlations (nonstabilizer structures) in complex many-body systems that are otherwise hidden by standard entanglement measures.
